#204's ruling (2026-08-05 decision session) declined to *rule* who reads a finished gate verdict and sent it here to be measured. This issue is that experiment.

## The task under test

Under #204, a subagent facing a foreseeably long gate commits, dispatches it detached, arms `just watch`, writes its handoff, and ends. Something then reads the result:

> Read `just watch-report` / `just verdict`. Branch on the class — green: land, or dispatch a landing agent. Red: dispatch a fresh agent with the failure bundle.

Most of the judgement is already discharged by the recipe: `just verdict` (#199) renders a finished pool's own record — worst class, counts, wall, sha, the runner's per-probe block verbatim — and "reads; never interprets". The open question is how cheap a seat can be and still get the branch right.

## Arms

**A:** the fable/high orchestrator — what happens today, and the interim while this runs.

**B**, all four, per the human's answer:

| Arm | Seat | Note |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | `cti-recon` (haiku/low) | read-only by definition, so it tests reading and reporting only — it cannot land or dispatch |
| B2 | `cti-mechanical` (sonnet/medium) | can land and dispatch, so it tests the whole branch |
| B3 | `cti-implementer` (opus/high) | control. If this fails the criterion, the cheaper arms need not be run |
| B4 | a dedicated verdict-reader seat | a new `.claude/agents/` definition scoped to this one job, carrying no implementation context |

Run B3 first as the control.

## Failure criterion

Ruled in the decision session, unamended. Any one of these fails that arm:

- misreading the worst class
- interpreting an `infra_unavailable` or `untyped_harness_failure` as a result
- landing on a red
- failing to quote SHA and evidence path into the issue the run gated

Choose the cheapest arm that clears it.

## Design notes

- The arms can run against **existing finished pools** under `~/.arma-cti/runs/`, so this does not need to wait on #204's landing or on fresh Arma tier time. Prefer replaying real evidence, including the awkward ones — #164's crash cluster (five attempts, only the fifth a result) and #149's three typed `infra_unavailable` stops are exactly the cases where a cheap seat would be expected to fail.
- A green pool is the majority case and the easy one. Weight the sample toward reds and toward not-a-result stops, or the experiment will conclude that every arm passes.
- Report the run count per arm and the arrangement, per the `flake_quarantine` row's discipline — a pass rate with no arrangement behind it is what #130 cost three rounds.

## Gate on the fourth arm

**Running** B4 as an experiment is approved. **Ratifying** a fifth seat into CLAUDE.md's Model roles mapping is a separate human sign-off, because that mapping is a standing human decision (2026-08-04). If B4 wins, propose it; do not land it.

## Interim this expires

The fable/high orchestrator reads, which is what happens today.

Refs #204, #199, #198, #203
